if Iphone use Cortex ARM then probably it affected, here is list of vulnerable ARMs https://developer.arm.com/support/security-update

The relevant features are out-of-order execution(where the processor looks at the upcoming demands and do them in any order it damn well pleases so long as they don't depend on unfinished calculations) and speculative execution(when there's an upcoming fork in the code, the processor predicts which one will be taken and works it while waiting for the final decision).

A processor lacking these two capabilities would generally be slower than one that does, but the Pi would've paid the price in the original design choice. As for the iPhone, they probably did use the more advanced(and vulnerable) chips.
Apple has also confirmed that the two vulnerabilities affect all Mac and iOS devices.
